source: Built-in generic example; REML, all-study correction, no covariate
plain: This analysis combined 7 studies of diagnostic test accuracy. Summary sensitivity was 0.811 (95% confidence interval 0.767 to 0.848), and summary specificity was 0.910 (0.886 to 0.929). Sensitivity describes detection among people with the condition; specificity describes negative tests among people without it. The plotted prediction region describes variation expected in a similar new study, whereas the confidence region describes uncertainty in the summary point. These results do not establish clinical usefulness or causation.
methods: The Reitsma bivariate model jointly pooled logit sensitivity and logit false-positive rate using restricted maximum likelihood (REML). Within-study variances were sums of reciprocal cell counts, with zero within-study covariance. Likelihood fits used iterated generalised least-squares initialisation followed by BFGS optimisation of Cholesky covariance parameters. If any cell was zero, 0.5 was added to every cell of every study. Summary 95% confidence limits used normal Wald intervals on the logit scale and inverse-logit back-transformation; specificity was the complement of the false-positive rate with interval endpoints reversed. Likelihood ratios were derived from the summary sensitivity and specificity; their log-scale Wald intervals used the delta method with the fitted covariance. The diagnostic odds ratio was the ratio of the positive and negative likelihood ratios. The 95% confidence and prediction regions were logit-scale ellipses centred at the summary point, using respectively its covariance V and V + Ψ, then inverse-logit transformed. Their squared radius was the chi-square quantile with 2 degrees of freedom (5.991465); no separate univariate prediction interval was computed. The Rutter–Gatsonis SROC and HSROC parameters were derived from the fitted means and between-study covariance. AUC used the mada grid convention: endpoint half-weights and interior weights summed and divided by 99, over false-positive rates 0.01 to 0.99; partial AUC used the same grid size over the observed uncorrected false-positive-rate range clipped to those bounds. The comparison Moses–Littenberg curve used unweighted ordinary least squares of the difference of the logits on their sum, after the selected correction. The threshold correlation was Spearman correlation between logit sensitivity and logit false-positive rate, with average ranks for ties. Deeks’ test regressed log diagnostic odds ratios on inverse square root effective sample size, weighted by effective sample size. Its slope used a two-sided t test with 5 residual degrees of freedom. For this test, 0.5 was added to all cells of each study containing a zero cell, independently of the bivariate correction choice. The Fagan display converted a pre-test probability of 20% to odds, multiplied by each summary likelihood ratio, then converted back to probabilities. The reported log-likelihood includes the logit-transformation Jacobian; AIC uses 5 parameters under the app’s mada convention, including covariance parameters even for a fixed-effect fit. Analyses were run in allmeta dta-sroc <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: Across 7 studies, summary sensitivity was 0.811 (95% CI 0.767 to 0.848) and specificity was 0.910 (0.886 to 0.929). LR+ was 9.01 (6.92 to 11.74); LR− was 0.21 (0.17 to 0.26); diagnostic OR was 43.4. Between-study variance was 0.0607 for logit sensitivity and 0.0506 for logit false-positive rate. Between-study correlation was −1.000. AUC was 0.932 (partial AUC 0.792). HSROC parameters were Λ = 3.8124, Θ = −0.5147, β = −0.0906, σ²θ = 0.0000, and σ²α = 0.2218. Log-likelihood was 26.97; AIC was −43.93. Moses intercept α = 4.309; slope β = 0.464. Spearman threshold correlation was −0.750. Deeks’ test p = 0.078. At 20% pre-test probability, the Fagan display gave post-test probabilities of 69% after a positive test and 5% after a negative test.
flags: With few studies, the between-study covariance and prediction region are imprecise, and Deeks’ small-study test is underpowered.
Absolute threshold correlation exceeds 0.6; the app flags a possible threshold effect. Interpret the SROC curve alongside the summary point.
